Sonnet 5 also introduces a new tokenizer that increases token counts by approximately 30%, effectively raising costs for some languages and code types. The update removes support for sampling parameters like temperature, top_p, and top_k, and enables adaptive thinking by default unless explicitly disabled. Despite the increased tokenization, Sonnet 5 maintains the same set of tools and platform features as its predecessor, Sonnet 4.6. The model's reduced capability in cyber tasks compared to Mythos 5 allowed its release without US government restrictions. Early tests show the new tokenizer results in higher token counts for English, Spanish, and Python code, while costs remain similar for Simplified Mandarin.

entry.title: RunInfra launches tool to optimize any open AI model down to the kernel and deploy it within five minutes
entry.summary: RunInfra has introduced a new tool designed to optimize any open AI model down to the kernel level and enable deployment within five minutes. This solution aims to streamline the process of enhancing AI model performance and simplify rapid deployment. By focusing on kernel-level optimization, the tool promises improved efficiency and faster integration for AI applications.

entry.title: Researchers demonstrate AI browsers can be tricked into ignoring safety guardrails by accepting false premises like 2 + 2 = 5, enabling potential data extraction attacks [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have demonstrated that AI browsers can be manipulated into ignoring their built-in safety guardrails by accepting false premises, such as the incorrect statement that 2 + 2 = 5. This manipulation lulls the AI into a false reality where it no longer enforces restrictions, potentially allowing attackers to extract sensitive data like private code or credentials. The proof-of-concept exploit involves a malicious website presenting a puzzle that rewards incorrect answers, causing the AI to enter this altered state and bypass its safety measures. This vulnerability highlights a fundamental issue with current AI browser guardrails, which are reactive and can be circumvented by changing the AI's context rather than addressing underlying risks. The technique, demonstrated on multiple AI browsers, raises concerns about the merging of browsing and AI assistant functions, which could lead to new vectors for data breaches and unauthorized actions. While the current exploit is more a demonstration than a stealthy attack, it underscores the need for more robust security approaches in AI browser design.

entry.title: Google launches Nano Banana 2 Lite, a faster and cheaper AI image generator optimized for high-volume workflows, available via Google AI Studio and Gemini API [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Google has launched Nano Banana 2 Lite, an updated AI image generator designed to be faster and more cost-effective, targeting high-volume workflows. Available through Google AI Studio and the Gemini API, this model produces images in about four seconds at a low cost, making it suitable for creators who need to generate and refine large numbers of images quickly. It serves as a replacement for the earlier Nano Banana model and complements Google's broader suite of generative media tools. Nano Banana 2 Lite builds on previous versions by offering lower latency and affordability, costing $0.034 per 1,000 images. This release follows Google's ongoing efforts to enhance AI-generated imagery, including the introduction of Nano Banana Pro for advanced use cases and the wider availability of Gemini Omni Flash for video generation. Google positions these tools as aids for creative iteration, particularly in advertising and multimedia production. The launch reflects continued investment in AI content generation despite some public criticism, with Google also recently partnering with indie studio A24. The company emphasizes the integration of rapid image creation with video editing capabilities to support comprehensive multimedia experiences for developers and creators.

entry.title: Google launches Gemini Spark for macOS with app integrations and real-time topic tracking, available in beta for AI Ultra subscribers in the US [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Google has launched Gemini Spark for macOS, now available in beta for AI Ultra subscribers in the US. The update enables users to automate tasks across desktop files, connect with popular apps like Canva and Dropbox, and track topics in real time for news, sports, and finance updates without manual refreshing. Gemini Spark on macOS allows users to remotely assign complex tasks from their phones and integrates with Google Workspace to streamline workflows. The app also supports new integrations with Google Tasks, Google Keep, Instacart, OpenTable, and Zillow Rentals, with plans to expand connected apps further. These enhancements aim to boost productivity by combining desktop automation with real-time information tracking and app connectivity.

entry.title: xAI launches Grok, an AI chatbot developed by its creators [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: xAI, the company behind the AI chatbot Grok, has officially launched the new chatbot developed by its creators. Grok is designed to provide advanced conversational AI capabilities, marking xAI's entry into the competitive AI chatbot market.

entry.title: Anthropic launches AI drug discovery program using Claude Science platform in June 2026
entry.summary: Anthropic has launched a new AI-driven drug discovery program utilizing its Claude Science platform as of June 2026. This initiative aims to accelerate the development of pharmaceuticals by leveraging advanced artificial intelligence technologies. The program represents a significant step in integrating AI capabilities into the pharmaceutical research and development process.

entry.title: Google launches TikTok-style 60-second AI video summaries in NotebookLM for AI Ultra and Pro subscribers, with free user support coming soon [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Google's NotebookLM has introduced a new feature that creates 60-second TikTok-style AI video summaries of users' notes, currently available to AI Ultra and Pro subscribers. These vertical clips combine AI-generated images and narration to summarize uploaded sources, enhancing how users interact with their research. Users can generate these videos by selecting the "Video" option in NotebookLM's Studio column and choosing a topic for the AI to focus on. The feature is initially available in English, with plans to extend support to free users soon.

entry.title: Etched, Nvidia AI chip competitor, reaches $5 billion valuation and books $1 billion in contract sales for inference systems [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Etched, a startup competing with Nvidia in the AI chip market, has reached a $5 billion valuation and secured $1 billion in contract sales for its inference systems. These systems, which include custom-designed racks and software alongside the chips, aim to improve the speed, cost, and power efficiency of running AI inference tasks. Founded in 2022, Etched recently completed manufacturing its chip with TSMC and is currently testing its product with customers. The company has raised a total of $800 million, including a $500 million round led by Stripes, and counts prominent investors and AI experts among its backers. Etched's focus on specialized chips addresses the growing demand for efficient AI inference, a critical bottleneck for scaling AI services.
